newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Greaves says sales jump in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: India's Greaves says sales jump in 96/97.

text.p: India's Greaves Ltd said on Thursday that turnover in 1996/97 (April-March) is approaching 10 billion rupees, already outstripping 1995/96 sales with almost two months remaining in the financial year.
The engineering arm of the Thapar group said in a statement that it "is already nearing the 10 billion rupee turnover mark this year".
In 1995/96, Greaves reported turnover of 7.30 billion rupees.
Greaves said it will launch 15 new products as part of a plan to increase turnover to 20 billion rupees in the year 2000.
The company is diversifying into the automobile industry and developing new products in its traditional engineering industry, it said.
Greaves is launching a 6-seater diesel three-wheeler vehicle, it said. Three-wheelers are widely used In India as taxis and to transport goods.
Greaves will make a tractor in technical collaboration with Italy's SAME, it said.
The company also plans to manufacture a new model diesel generating set as well as new types of gear boxes, diesel engines and construction equipment.
